answer: Every die leaves the foundry with its key fused shut, so a copied head owns a key that fits no slot. Work counts only as a whisper the knoll signs after matching the head's key to a seated die, one thread per die, and metering that thread's draw. Each epoch an operator is billed base times the most threads it ran concurrently, and every knoll meters its own seats, so no split across hosts washes the peak out. To hold k clones the attacker wires k dies and pays base×k each epoch; a newcomer with one die draws base once.
